label: House land share in realm
summary: Whether the share of counties the house holds in a top liege's realm compares as given.
details: Only direct vassals of the top liege count. A house member who holds land but is not a direct vassal counts as holding none. Only rulers with the same government type as the top liege are counted. The game's documentation calls the result a percentage, but its own example compares against 0.5, so the value is probably a fraction (0.5 = half).

fields.name: target
fields.text: The top liege whose realm is measured.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The share to compare against, written with a comparison.

label: House power
summary: Whether the house's power compares as given.
details: Written as a comparison on a house, e.g. house_power >= value. The game does not say here how house power is calculated.

label: House unity
summary: Whether the house's unity value compares as given.
details: Vanilla compares it against named thresholds such as critical_house_unity, decent_house_unity and very_high_house_unity, using >, >=, < or <=.

label: Important action dismissed
summary: Whether an important action is available to the character but they dismissed it.
details: Write the key of the important action after the equals sign.

label: Important action shown
summary: Whether the given important action is currently shown to the character.
details: Write the key of the important action after the equals sign. Compare with important_action_is_valid_but_invisible, the dismissed case.

label: In diplomatic range
summary: Whether the character and the given character are within each other's diplomatic range.
details: The game's documentation words it as each within the other's range. Vanilla gives it a character, often root or a saved scope such as scope:owner or scope:attacker.

label: Influence
summary: Whether the character's influence compares as given.
details: Vanilla mostly compares against named values such as medium_influence_value or major_influence_value, or influence cost values. It can also be a block with value and multiply: vanilla uses it with value = scope:actor.monumental_influence_value and multiply = 2, which appears to scale the value before comparing (an inference; the game's documentation does not describe the block).

fields.name: value
fields.values: a number, script value or named value

fields.name: multiply
fields.text: Seen in vanilla's block form, where it is 2; apparently a factor applied to the value.

label: Influence level
summary: Whether the character's influence level compares as given.
details: Vanilla compares it with whole numbers, mostly 3 or more, and once with the named value high_influence_level.

label: Innovation era
summary: Whether the innovation belongs to the given era.
details: Works on an innovation, e.g. scope:innovation = { innovation_era = culture_era_early_medieval }.

label: Innovation is regional
summary: Whether the innovation is a regional one.
details: Write yes or no. Works on an innovation.

label: Innovation is
summary: Whether the innovation is the given one.
details: Write the innovation's key, e.g. gunpowder. Works on an innovation.

label: Gold invested in inspiration
summary: Whether the amount of gold invested in the inspiration compares as given.
details: Works on an inspiration, e.g. inspiration_gold_invested > 5.

label: Inspiration progress
summary: Whether the inspiration's progress compares as given.
details: Vanilla uses it with plain numbers, e.g. > 1 and < 10.

label: Intrigue skill
summary: Whether the character's intrigue skill compares as given.
details: Vanilla compares against named ratings such as high_skill_rating, decent_skill_rating and very_high_skill_rating, or plain numbers like 10 or 12.

label: Intrigue difference
summary: Whether the difference between the character's intrigue skill and another character's compares as given.
details: The game's documentation does not say which skill is subtracted from which. Vanilla uses it with targets such as liege or scope:vizier and values like >= 5 or >= -5. The game's documentation says abs = yes ignores the sign of the difference (default no); that reading of abs is an inference from its name. The documented usage line is headed intrigue, but the key is intrigue_diff.

fields.name: target
fields.values: a character, e.g. liege or scope:vizier

fields.name: value
fields.text: The difference to compare against, written with a comparison.
fields.values: a comparison such as >= 5 or >= -5 (can be negative)

fields.name: abs
fields.text: Whether to use the absolute difference (inferred from the name).

label: Intrigue for portrait
summary: Whether the character's intrigue skill, scaled to between 0.0 and 1.0, compares as given.
details: The game's documentation says the scaling is meant for portraits. The input shows no vanilla use.

label: Intrigue perk points
summary: Whether the number of perk points the character has available compares as given.
details: Vanilla compares it against max_perk_amount_per_lifestyle. The game's documentation says only 'perk points available'; that these are the intrigue lifestyle's points is an inference from the key name.

label: Intrigue perks owned
summary: Whether the number of perks the character has from the intrigue lifestyle compares as given.
details: The game's documentation says 'from this lifestyle'; that this means the intrigue lifestyle is read from the key name.

label: Intrigue perks unlockable
summary: Whether the number of intrigue lifestyle perks the character can unlock right now compares as given.
details: It checks that the character has the parent perks and that the perk's can_be_picked condition is met. It does not check perk points.

label: Intrigue lifestyle XP
summary: Whether the character's experience in the intrigue lifestyle compares as given.
details: The game's documentation text is copied from the perk points trigger and says 'perk points available', which does not match the name. This explanation goes by the key name.

label: Is faction leader
summary: Whether the character leads a faction.
details: Write yes or no. Vanilla uses it mostly as no.

label: Is faction member
summary: Whether the character is a member of a faction.
details: Write yes or no. The game's documentation does not say whether a faction's leader counts as a member.

label: Travel plan aborted
summary: Whether the travel plan was aborted.
details: Write yes or no. Works on a travel plan.

label: Fit to succeed accolade
summary: Whether the character is an acceptable fit to take over as the given accolade's successor.
details: Give it the accolade, e.g. scope:accolade_in_need. The game's documentation does not say what makes a character acceptable.

label: Is acclaimed knight
summary: Whether the character is the acclaimed knight of an accolade.
details: Write yes or no.

label: Is accolade successor
summary: Whether the character is the successor of an accolade.
details: Write yes or no.

label: Active relic for holy site
summary: Whether the artifact can benefit the given holy site, meaning it is a relic of the faith that controls that site.
details: Give it the holy site, e.g. scope:holy_site. Works on an artifact.

label: Is active tax obligation
summary: Whether the given obligation is the tax slot's current active tax obligation.
details: Write the obligation's key. Works on a tax slot.

label: Activity is complete
summary: Whether the activity has been completed.
details: The game says it rarely matters for content because activities are deleted as soon as possible. In multiplayer an activity lives until everyone stops viewing it, so this is used to cancel some delayed events. Write yes or no.

label: Activity type on cooldown
summary: Whether the given activity type is on cooldown for the character.
details: Write the activity type's key, such as activity_feast. Vanilla uses it with many activity types.

label: Next to clerical region
summary: Whether the given title has at least one county, not already in a clerical region, that borders this clerical region.
details: It fails if the title it runs on is not a clerical region title. Give it the title to check, e.g. scope:title.

label: Is adult
summary: Whether the character is an adult.
details: Write yes or no. no means the character is not an adult.

label: Exposed agent in scheme
summary: Whether the character is an exposed agent in the given scheme.
details: Give it the scheme, e.g. scope:scheme.

label: Agent slot type
summary: Whether the agent slot is of the given type.
details: Write the type's key. Vanilla uses types such as agent_thief, agent_assassin and agent_lookout.

label: Ahead of time for culture
summary: Whether the innovation belongs to a later era than the given culture's current era.
details: The game's documentation says it is the same as checking that the innovation's era is above the culture's era. Give it the culture, e.g. scope:culture.

label: Is AI
summary: Whether the character is played by the AI.
details: Write yes or no. no means the AI does not play the character.

label: Is alive
summary: Whether the character is alive.
details: Write yes or no. no means the character is dead.

label: Allied in a war
summary: Whether the character is allied to the given character in a war.
details: Give it the other character, e.g. scope:liege.

label: Is allied to
summary: Whether the character is allied to the given character.
details: Give it the other character, e.g. root or scope:actor.

label: Army in combat
summary: Whether the army is currently in combat.
details: Write yes or no. Works on an army.
